chunks: Saad ibn Abdullah narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn Miskan, from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) kept his message concealed in Mecca, hiding and fearful, for five years, not publicizing it, while Ali (peace be upon him) and Khadija were with him. Then Allah, the Exalted, commanded him to announce what he was ordered to do, so he appeared and publicized his matter.
ai.seo_question: How long did the Prophet Muhammad keep his message concealed in Mecca before announcing it publicly?
ai.summary: This narration from *Kitab al-Ghayba* highlights the strategic period of *Kitman al-Dawlah* (concealment of the state) in Mecca, where the Prophet, accompanied by Imam Ali and Khadija, practiced caution to consolidate the core message before facing Quraysh's opposition. This five-year interval serves as a historical precedent for the Imam's own delayed reappearance, illustrating that concealment is not merely a passive absence but a calculated phase of divine preparation and protection.
